summary: Every turn that could have spoken now files a readable determination — including the ones nobody had a way to read.
details: A determination — the occasion, the room, the verdict, what she would have said and the window she read it against — is now a value with two sinks: the shadow mirror it always had, and the process log, which needs no channel and costs no send.
The proactive act turn's restraint (design 39 D12) is readable for the first time: it had a counter and a row saying silent, and nothing that said what it declined.
A participation determination in a room with no operator-wired mirror is now readable too; previously it was readable nowhere at all.
The shape goes to INFO and the speech to DEBUG, as two fixed-shape events — the same split the fire path already made for unrouted prose, so group speech does not enter the log at INFO.
limitations: The shadow mirror's own output is unchanged, and it remains participation-only: this adds a second reader, not a second mirror.
Reading a determination's draft or the window it closed on requires the deployment to be at DEBUG.
